action.action-desc: Ms. Tlaib (for herself, Ms. Ansari, Mr. Carson, Mrs. Fletcher, Mr. García of Illinois, Ms. Garcia of Texas, Mrs. Grijalva, Ms. Hoyle of Oregon, Mr. Johnson of Georgia, Ms. Kamlager-Dove, Mr. Krishnamoorthi, Mr. Landsman, Mr. Larson of Connecticut, Ms. Lee of Pennsylvania, Mrs. McClain Delaney, Mr. McGarvey, Mr. Menefee, Ms. Ocasio-Cortez, Mrs. Ramirez, Ms. Randall, Ms. Salinas, Ms. Simon, Mr. Thanedar, Ms. Velázquez, Mrs. Watson Coleman, and Ms. Williams of Georgia) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Homeland Security, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to prohibit the Secretary of Homeland Security from accessing or utilizing certain information to carry out certain functions of U.S. Customs and Border Protection or U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and from carrying out certain actions regarding Trusted Traveler programs, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the No TSA Data for ICE Act.

section.header: Prohibitions regarding information sharing and Trusted Traveler programs

subsection.text: Title VII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 341 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

section.header: Prohibitions regarding information sharing and Trusted Traveler programs

subsection.text: The Secretary may neither access nor utilize, whether through direct means or indirect means, such as Mobile Fortify or another similar application, specified information to carry out a function of any of the following:

paragraph.text: The Secretary may not deny, suspend, or early terminate an individual’s enrollment in a program specified in paragraph (2) on the basis of such individual’s participation in an activity protected by the First Amendment to the Constitution of the United States.
A program specified in this paragraph is any of the following:

subparagraph.text: The PreCheck Program under section 44919 of title 49, United States Code.
The Global Entry, SENTRI, and FAST programs under subsection (k) of section 7208 of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (8 U.S.C. 1365b).
The NEXUS program under section 404 of the Enhanced Border Security and Visa Entry Reform Act of 2002 (8 U.S.C. 1753).
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Business Travel Card program under section 418.

subsection.text: In this section, the term specified information means any of the following:

paragraph.text: Information from the Transportation Security Administration.
Data that satisfies the following requirements:

subparagraph.text: Includes personally identifiable information of a flight passenger.
Is from a private sector entity that brokers such data.

subsection.text: The table of contents in section 1(b) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 713 the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: Sec. 714. Prohibitions regarding information sharing and Trusted Traveler programs.
